$comment: The external executables used by the photo and encoding tools. tools:check reads
declarations, probes their locations, and compares reported versions. Cloudflare
and GitHub state belongs in config/infra.json.
required_by names callers; optional allows a missing executable. Read each
optional_why: zenc is built on demand, while AVIF callers have different fallback
rules. path is absolute or repository-relative; without it, the check searches
PATH. These are the checker locations, so compare them with the caller before
concluding that a version difference affects an output.
version declares the flag and output pattern, or reports:false with a reason.
Named capture groups preserve linked components such as libavif plus AOM and
zenc plus zenjpeg. A multi-component pattern cannot carry min_version because
those records have no single numeric ordering.
bytes marks executables that produce artifact bytes. recorded is the reviewed
version comparison baseline; a difference is advisory, while an unreadable
version or violated minimum fails. Matching versions alone do not prove
artifact provenance: source, flags, and inputs matter too. Metrics marked
bytes:false can still influence quality selection and need review when changed.
Historical controls: recorded began as a workstation observation on 2026-08-24.
The 2026-08-28 pixel-tier rerender reproduced all 165 JPEGs byte-for-byte and
reproduced three old AVIF tiles at --speed 4 before taking --speed 2. The same
flag study found --jobs 1 differed from parallel encoding, while 2, 4, and 8
agreed on those inputs. On 2026-09-27, aom 3.15.0 and 3.15.1 (swapped under one
zenc and one avifenc binary) reproduced 36 of 36 shipped 4:4:4 tiers on 9 stems
and 6 of 6 CLI encodes on macOS arm64. Preserve these as scoped measurements, not a guarantee
for a different source, encoder, or configuration.
Grid ingest and rerenders link the INSTALLED libavif through zenc. The
zenc-avif entry records the library actually loaded by that binary; avifenc
remains the reference CLI and serves cars and encoding studies. No grid
fallback selects a different encoder. The installed library follows the
owner preference of 2026-09-12; recorded versions detect drift without
claiming provenance for already shipped tiles. Update recorded only with
reviewed artifact evidence. docs/DEPENDENCIES.md describes the checks and
docs/MAINTENANCE.md the procedures.

tools.why: every EXIF read and write in the pipeline. It emits metadata.json's record shape directly and owns the merge, which retired the 50-line jq reshape and build-recipes.py, and on 2026-08-14 it took the last of exiftool's jobs too: orientation reads, -all= strips and -TagsFromFile copies, in ExifTool's own flag spellings. Pinned at 0.4.0 by the guards in the writing scripts: 0.1.0 could not write, and its -all= truncated progressive JPEGs at the first scan, which is every JPEG this pipeline produces; 0.2.0's -TagsFromFile carried a HEIF's EXIF and silently dropped its XMP item, the only place an X-T50 records an in-camera star rating (oddharsh/exif-sooc#3); and before 0.4.0 it could not read or write a JPEG XL, which a HIF photo's archive is since 2026-10 and which needs the HIF's own EXIF copied on, because sips keeps 40 of its 75 tags and none of the Fujifilm maker notes (oddharsh/exif-sooc#4)
resize, HEIF decode, and the AVIF fallback encoder
pulls the R2 originals back down
tools.bytes_why: moves bytes it did not make

tools.why: builds zenc, the shipped JPEG encoder, on first run
tools.bytes_why: builds zenc, and zenjpeg's encode is deterministic for a given pin, which dependabot owns in tools/photos/zenc/Cargo.toml. A compiler bump does not move a JPEG, and it does not move a HISTOGRAM either, which is the half that was doubted: `bun run zenc:reproducible` bakes all 165 stems under three rustc versions and diffs them

tools.why: configures and builds the pinned AVIF encoder and its libraries
tools.bytes_why: build orchestration; the encoder source and build configuration live in tools/photos/libavif/build.sh

tools.why: executes the CMake build for the pinned AVIF encoder
tools.bytes_why: runs the declared build commands; does not encode images

tools.why: fetches the pinned AVIF encoder sources; also supplies the tracked-script census for tools:check
tools.bytes_why: retrieves source bytes and reads repository ownership; does not encode images

tools.why: JPEG and AVIF grid encoder, square/resize geometry, and histogram bake; grid callers build incrementally and require installed libavif development files
tools.optional_why: `optional` here means BUILT ON DEMAND rather than degrades: every caller runs `cargo build --release --locked` when the binary is missing, so an absent zenc on a fresh checkout is a state the pipeline repairs itself rather than a prerequisite anybody has to go install. A missing `cargo` is the blocking failure, and cargo is declared above

BUILT ON DEMAND like zenc: hif-archive.ts and photo-metrics.ts run the install command on their first score in a process, and export-for-instagram.sh runs it when the binary is missing, so an absent binary on a fresh checkout is repaired rather than installed by hand. A missing `cargo` is the blocking failure, and cargo is declared above
tools.why: SSIMULACRA2 (fast-ssim2) and butteraugli (imazen's port) in one process, for every photo tool that scores: the bar a HIF photo's JPEG XL archive has to clear (hif-archive.ts, since 2026-10-14), the Instagram export's quality search, and the probes and page generators through photo-metrics.ts (since 2026-10-31). Each replaced libjxl's ssimulacra2 and butteraugli_main after the same decisions came back both ways

version.why: prints no version; the fast-ssim2 and butteraugli pins are exact in tools/photos/photo-metrics/Cargo.toml and its Cargo.lock, which is the identity an archive decision is made against

tools.bytes_why: decides the encoder distance of every HIF archive it scores, so a metric change can change archive bytes: a pin move is a re-measurement against libjxl (Cargo.toml says how)

tools.optional_why: BUILT ON DEMAND like photo-metrics: hif-archive.ts and photo-metrics-parity.ts run the install command before their first encode in a process, so an absent binary on a fresh checkout is repaired rather than installed by hand. A missing `cargo` is the blocking failure, and cargo is declared above
tools.why: every lossy encode of a HIF photo's archive: jixel at Speed::Slow with progressive DC, which beat cjxl -e 7 -p at matched ssimulacra2 and butteraugli on 8 of 8 HIFs (median -2.6%, -5.0% bytes-weighted, 2026-10-17) and keeps its 8 to 11 KB first paint. It also carries the PNG's eXIf orientation into the codestream and its Exif into a raw box, which exif-sooc needs. cjxl still makes every lossless repack

version.why: prints no version; the jixel pin is exact in tools/photos/jixel-enc/Cargo.toml and its Cargo.lock, which is the identity an archive is encoded with

tools.bytes_why: writes the bytes of every HIF archive that beats its bar, so a jixel move changes archive bytes and distances: a pin move is a re-measurement (rerun hif-archive.ts on a few HIFs against their bars, and recheck the first paint)

tools.why: timbrado's Rust measurement engine (0.2.0): runs every upstream watch under the pinned bun and the candidate, in a scratch directory it removes; the TypeScript half (reporter, digest, survey, resolve) needs no binary
tools.optional_why: BUILT ON DEMAND like zenc: `ensureTimbradoEngine` in tools/lib/upstream-watches.ts runs the install command whenever a watch is read and throws when it cannot, so an absent engine on a fresh checkout is repaired rather than installed by hand, and a runner without cargo is exit 2 rather than eight rows reading `null`. The path is inside node_modules because bun lays the git dependency out per commit sha, so a pin bump is a fresh directory and the build follows it. `TIMBRADO_BIN` names a built engine elsewhere and skips the build
tools.bytes_why: supervises probe processes and parses their JSON line; encodes nothing and touches no served byte

tools.why: progressive rearrangement of the R2 share copies, a coefficient reorder. It did EXIF-orientation rotation until 2026-08-26; that is `zenc square --orient` now, per docs/GOTCHAS.md gotcha 3
the chroma-subsampling row of the /garage/encoding grids

decodes each Instagram export candidate for photo-metrics, which reads PNG and PNM only. libjpeg-turbo is the decoder libjxl's ssimulacra2 linked, so the scores did not move: 84.89105760 from ssimulacra2 on the JPEG and on djpeg's PPM alike (2026-10-31)
AVIF command-line reference for car images and encoding studies; grid ingest uses the installed library through zenc
tools.bytes_why: Produces AVIF artifacts for cars and encoding studies; the native grid path uses the same installed library. /i/ is content-addressed, so a version change here re-mints nothing already shipped and decides the bytes of what is added next.

tools.why: each full-resolution original that is not encoded from a HIF, a lossless JPEG XL transcode (--lossless_jpeg=1 -e 9) of the JPEG it replaces in R2, and the repack a HIF archive is scored against and falls back to. jixel-enc makes the HIF-born ones
the original's proof: it rebuilds the JPEG from the .jxl, which uploads only if cmp finds the rebuilt bytes identical; the remote pipeline uses it to get the JPEG back for its encoders
tools.bytes_why: Decode only. It rebuilds a JPEG that zenc and exif-sooc read, and that JPEG is the exact one the .jxl was made from, whatever the djxl version.

tools.why: the WebP point on the /garage/encoding format grid
tools.bytes_why: Produces the WebP comparison samples in public/garage/enc. The photo grid has JPEG and AVIF tiers.

tools.optional_why: the ORACLE and nothing else: photo-metrics-parity.ts checks photo-metrics against it before a pin move. Every caller moved to photo-metrics by 2026-10-31, so a photo session without it loses nothing
tools.why: libjxl's SSIMULACRA2, the reference photo-metrics is measured against. brew's jpeg-xl bottle builds with JPEGXL_ENABLE_DEVTOOLS=ON and ships it (0.12.0, checked 2026-10-31)

version.why: This libjxl metric prints usage instead of exposing a version flag. Record the jpeg-xl version beside a parity run, since it is the reference that run reads.

tools.optional_why: the ORACLE and nothing else, beside ssimulacra2 above
tools.why: libjxl's butteraugli, the reference photo-metrics is measured against. Ships in the same brew bottle as ssimulacra2

version.why: This libjxl metric has no version flag. Record the jpeg-xl version beside a parity run, as for ssimulacra2.

tools.why: resolves installed libavif development headers and libraries for the native grid encoder
tools.bytes_why: build discovery; the linked libavif and AOM versions decide AVIF bytes

tools.install: brew install libavif pkgconf; cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path tools/photos/zenc/Cargo.toml
tools.optional_why: zenc is built incrementally by grid callers before processing inputs
tools.why: records the installed libavif and AOM used for normal grid AVIF output

tools.install: brew install aom cmake ninja pkgconf && bun run av2:build
tools.optional_why: measurement only: codec-knob-probe.ts --codec avm is its one caller and refuses with the build command when it is missing. Nothing in the photo pipeline or the build needs it
tools.why: AV2 (AVM 1.0.0) still-image encoder, with avifdec beside it, for the --codec avm arm of codec-knob-probe.ts. Built from the av2-tone checkout package.json pins (github.com/oddharsh/av2-tone), which pins libavif by commit with its experimental AVIF_CODEC_AVM on
tools.bytes_why: writes scratch AV2 encodes for a probe and commits nothing; no browser decodes AV2, so none of its output can ship
